chapter: Kenton, Granz, Parker and the jazz clubs
title: Dexter Gordon, Brew Moore, Griffin and Herbie Mann
summary: Horn players who joined the band at the Ebony Club and Birdland, and the State Department trip.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: With Machito.
Machito. Dexter Gordon played with us in the Ebony Club. He got arrested.
Arrested.
And then he was so (inaudible). And then they brought a guy named Blue Moore (phonetic) to play with him.
Right, he was a tenor player.
Tenor player from Georgia. He disappeared. And then --
That -- you recorded Cuba City with him and Howard McGee, right?
Yeah. Then they brought --
When you say they, you mean Granz or who brought?

(MORRIS LEY Inaudible) said, Mario, I've got an idea. You don't mind to play with every man. Nobody know every man yet. I said, well, I don't mind. So they brought every man, this tenor player from Paris, I never seen --
John Baez?
No, Philip -- what's the name -- Griffin?
Oh, Johnny Griffin?

And that big trombone player, short, Black fellow, what's the name? Fuller, Fuller something, let me see the name, get back to -- so, all right, I take this fellow with me to the Birdland for two week engagement. It was a big hit. So MORRIS Murray say, let's record it. So we made an album with Herbie Mann. I made an album with Herbie Mann -- when that was made? I've got to (inaudible).

So to make the whole story short, then I'm supposed to go abroad to (THROUGH THE STATE DEPARTMENT inaudible). This when I got my lesson. I turn around, and they took Doc Cheetam from my band (inaudible).
Curtis Fuller
Doc Cheetam (inaudible)?
No, PATATO and Manguale, Doc Cheetam, the trumpet player.
Oh, yeah, right. And Herbie Mann took the trip (inaudible) took the trip as an Afro-Cuban band. They went to Africa. Yeah, just, okay --
(Interruption.)
